subject: Renewal conversion: staggered flex transition + scheduled fallback plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bowen <sarah@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversion: staggered flex transition + scheduled fallback plan

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our convo, I pulled together a concise proposal to move Nimbus from the current annual reserved commitment into a staggered ‘flex’ conversion with an embedded fallback (canary) so you keep predictable capacity during peak Q1 traffic. Attached is a short proposal (PDF) and a canary schedule (spreadsheet). High level: 

- Year 1: Convert 60% of committed tokens to the Flex bucket to reduce immediate cash outlay; keep 40% reserved to guarantee baseline throughput.
- Canary safety: For the first 8 weeks post-go-live we hold a mirrored dedicated pool that auto-fails open to a compatible model variant if latency or error budgets are exceeded.
- Auto-renew: Option to auto-renew flex at 6-month intervals with a 30-day opt-out to avoid mid-year co-term complexity.
- Price: blended token rate shown in the PDF with a 6% discount on reserved baseline.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm procurement contact to loop in (I included Tom).
2) We (Redwood) provide a final contract appendix with the canary SLAs and rollback triggers for legal to review (ready in 48 hours once you confirm scope).
3) Schedule an ops runbook review with Camila to finalize the failover playbook (30 minutes).

If this looks broadly right, I’ll ask Camila and Karthik to draft the appendix and the technical canary plan.

Thanks — talk soon.

Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood_renewal_proposal_Nimbus_v3.pdf (PDF), canary_schedule_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Sarah Bowen <sarah@nimhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimhealth.com>, Procure Team <procure@nimhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversion: staggered flex transition + scheduled fallback plan

Diego —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the materials. Overall the structure makes sense; a couple of clarifying questions from procurement/ops: 

- On the 8-week canary: what are the exact rollback triggers (errors/sec, 95th latency threshold, or token cost delta)? We need those to match our internal incident criteria.
- For the blended token rate: can we see an alternate that assumes a Q1 traffic spike (40% higher tokens) and the projected cost delta if the canary routes to fallback model for 2 weeks?
- Co-terming: we want the renewal to align with our Jan 1 fiscal window; how disruptive is the 6-month auto-renew opt-out to achieving a full co-term on Jan 1?

Looping Tom (ops) and procurement. If you can get answers before Friday, we can fast-track sign-off.

—Sarah
Director of Platform Ops
Nimbus Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bowen <sarah@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimhealth.com>, Procure Team <procure@nimhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversion: staggered flex transition + scheduled fallback plan

Sarah / Tom —

Good questions. Quick answers and next steps (we’ll put precise numbers in the appendix):

- Rollback triggers (proposed):
  * Error rate: >5x baseline errors/sec sustained for 5 minutes
  * Latency: 95th percentile exceeds target by >250ms for 10 consecutive minutes
  * Cost anomaly: projected token spend >20% above forecast over a 24-hour rolling window

- Cost-sensitivity scenario: Karthik will model a +40% Q1 traffic uplift with the canary routing to fallback for 14 days; expect a modest bump (we estimate +7–11% on total Q1 spend depending on fallback ratio). He’ll attach the scenario spreadsheet by EOD Thursday.

- Co-term / auto-renew alignment: The 6-month auto-renew window is optional — you can elect a one-time calendar alignment amendment so the contract co-terms to Jan 1 at execution. The opt-out is preserved at the 6-month mark after that alignment. In short: we can get you to a Jan 1 co-term without blocking the canary safety.

Camila — can you draft the technical canary runbook and the failback playbook with explicit triggers and rollback steps? Karthik — please add the cost scenario by Thursday. I’ll assemble a short appendix for legal.

Diego
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Bowen <sarah@nimhealth.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimhealth.com>, Procure Team <procure@nimhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversion: staggered flex transition + scheduled fallback plan

Diego / team —

Draft canary runbook (summary) below — I’ll push the full runbook into the shared Drive folder and link it in the appendix.

Canary runbook (summary):
- Duration: 8 weeks (with two-week review gates at week 2 and week 6).
- Metrics to monitor (real-time): 95p latency, errors/sec (5m aggregate), model quality drift (tiered prompt eval set), token consumption variance.
- Automated actions:
  1) <Alerting> If any trigger fires, send immediate page and open incident (PagerDuty).
  2) <Failover> If trigger persists for >10 mins, route new sessions to fallback model variant (same architecture, lower memory/resolution quantize).
  3) <Scale> If token burn > forecast but latency stable, enable burst pool for 2 hours while we assess.
- Manual checkpoints: Ops review at week 2 and week 6; legal & procurement sign-off on any extension beyond 8 weeks.

I’m tagging legal to prep the appendix language for the triggers and rollback. I’ll also add a short checklist for the customer-run smoke tests during cutover.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bowen <sarah@nimhealth.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimhealth.com>, Procure Team <procure@nimhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Final: proposed appendix + go/no-go checklist for Dec/Jan canary

Sarah / Tom —

Per the internal reviews, attached is the proposed appendix that codifies the rollback triggers, the 8-week canary plan, and a one-time calendar alignment clause to co-term with your Jan 1 window. Summary of asks for Nimbus: 

- Confirm: you approve the one-time calendar alignment to Jan 1 (this will co-term the contract on execution).
- Confirm: procurement will accept the rollback triggers listed in the attached appendix.
- Book: 30-minute ops runbook review next week (Camila suggested Wed 11am PT / your timezone).

If we get approvals by Tuesday EOD, legal will issue the contract appendix and we can target a Jan 2 soft cutover with an 8-week canary starting that day. Otherwise we’ll push the cutover to Jan 15 to respect procurement timelines.

Thanks again — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
